 JUDGMENT

This is a suit for permanent injunction by restraining the defendant, their men, agents, contractors,
workers or anybody claiming and acting under the defendants from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule property by the plaintiffs.

2. Brief facts of the plaintiffs case is that, the plaintiffs are the absolute owners in peaceful possession and enjoyment of Site bearing No.298, Khatha No.262/262/261/298, Vijaya Bank Employee Housing Co-operative Society Limited Layout, Bilekahalli, Begur Hobli, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: The self acquired property of the plaintiffs, they purchased the same as per registered sale deed dated 12.11.2014 vide document No.BNR-1-05562-2014-15, Book No.1, stored in CD No.BGRD254 in the office of the Sub- registrar, Jayanagar, Bengaluru.
After purchase the khatha was O.S.No.8098/2015 transferred in the names of plaintiffs as per khatha registration No.KTR/154/2015-16.
The BBMP assigned the khatha No.262/262/261/268 to the schedule property issued by the BBMP.
The plaintiffs have also paid taxes to the concerned authorities.
3. It is further submitted that, the plaintiffs have purchased the schedule property from one Ramesh Shetty S/o Gopala Shetty.
The Vijaya Bank Employees Housing Co-Operative Society Ltd formed a layout of sites by obtaning approved layout plan from the Bengaluru Development Authority.

sentences.text: The site No.298 is the part and parcel of the layout formed by the said society.
The vendor of the plaintiffs were allotted with the said site as he was the member of the said Society.
The said society also issued possession certificate dated 28.02.1994 to the vendor of the plaintiffs.

It is executed a registered sale deed in favour of the vendor as per sale deed 28.02.1994 vide document Ramakantha Shetty P vs Srinivas on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80287660/

Subsequently the measurements of the site which was allotted to the said vendor was not available on the spot and hence the said society executed a rectification deed dated 06.10.2007 vide document No.BMH-1-03804-2007-08 stored in CD No.BMHD332 registered before Sub-Registrar, Bommanahalli, Bengaluru.
The plaintiffs have not executed any O.S.No.8098/2015 registered or unregistered document either in favour of the defendants or in favour of any their parties in respect of the schedule property.
The defendant No.1, 2 and 4 are brothers and they are the children of the defendant No.3.
They are total strangers to the schedule property and they have no manner of right, title and interest over the schedule property.
The defendants are claiming that they are the owners of the property situated on Western side of the schedule property.

The defendants without obtaining any plan or license from the competent authority are illegally making attempts to construct a building on the property situated on the western side of the suit schedule property and The caused of action for this suit arose on dated 18.09.2015 the defendant No.1 to 3 came near the Western adjacent property and they were taking measurements and in the said process they have attempted to encroach upon the schedule property on the Western side to an extent of 15 feet.
The The plaintiffs questioned the defendants about their authority and also informed about their right over the schedule property.
However they proclaimed and threatened to the effect that they will dig in the schedule property on the Western side.
But the defendants threatened that they will continue their illegal acts and they will come back with more men and material.
The plaintiffs also approached the police but he police failed to O.S.No.8098/2015 assist the plaintiffs as the matter is of civil nature.
The plaintiffs apprehend that the defendants may come at any time and encroach upon the schedule property and they may put up construction by encroaching upon the schedule property.
If they succeed in their attempts the loss and hardship caused to the plaintiffs cannot be compensated in terms of money.
Hence, this suit.
4. After receipt of the suit summons, the defendants appeared through their counsel.
The defendant No.3 filed written statement.
The defendant Nos.1, 2 and 4 have adopted the written statement of defendant No.3.
The defendant No.3 filed written statement contending that, the averments made in para No.1 to 9 are denied as false in toto.
It is further contended that the suit is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
The family members of defendants are the owners in possession of Sy.No.112/11A and 112/12A situated at Belekahalli Village, Begur Hobli, Bengaluru south Taluk.
The same is their ancestral property.
It is submitted that the above said lands were not acquired by the Government in favour of the Vijaya Bank House Building Co-operative Society.

The plaintiffs are relying upon concocted and created documents and hence they are not entitled to any relief much less the one sought for in the suit.

sentences.text: As per defendants version Sy.No.112/11A and 112/12A situated at Bilekahalli Village, existed much prior to the issuance O.S.No.8098/2015 of notifications under Section 4(1), 6(1) and 16(2) of the land Acquisition Act and the said lands was not acquired and the Government Inform of the Vijaya Bank.

While perusing MFA No.12208/2007 dated 14.08.2008 in Ex.P.17 at Para 5, Page 4, it held as follows:-
"It is seen from the Preliminary Notification dated 30.05.1983 issued under section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, that an extent of 38 guntas was proposed to be guntas was proposed to acquired in Sy.No.112/12.
Land bearing Sy.Nos.112/11A and 112/12A were not mentioned as lands situated adjoining the lands proposed for acquisition.
This is evident from the boundaries mentioned in the notification in respect of the lands bearing Sy.Nos.112/11 and 112/12.
It is thus clear that at the time when the notification was issued in the year 1983, there was no land bearing Sy.Nos.112/11A and 112/12A situated, adjoining Sy.Nos.112/11 and 112/12.

After the O.S.No.8098/2015 Preliminary Notification, the owners of the land proposed to be acquired appeared to have made a representation to the acquiring body requesting for deletion of their lands or atleast the constructed portion in the land from the acquisition.

Based on this representation, while issuing the final notification dated 01.06.1985, only an extent of 27 guntas was acquired in Sy.No.112/11 excluding 11 guntas and in so far as Sy.No.112/12 is concerned, only an extent of 12 guntas came to be acquired excluding an extent of 15 guntas.
In the final notification, for the first time Sy.Nos.112/12A and 112/11A were shown as lands situated adjoining the acquired lands.
When the sub-division of these lands took place creating Sy.Nos.112/12A and 112/11A is not forthcoming from the records produced by the authorities.

sentences.text: The plaintiff who asserts his right, title and interest over these properties is not in a position to show how and when the sub- O.S.No.8098/2015 numbers were assigned.

It is to be stated here that for effecting any phodi or division, there will be necessarily mutation by the revenue authorities and the best way to establish such sub-division was by producing such a mutation entry.

In the absence of such a mutation entry,
this Court called upon the appellant herein to produce the RTC extracts of Sy.No.112/11A and 112/12A as it existed prior to 1983.

This direction was issued as it was asserted at the time of arguments that the phodi was conducted long back and the sub-division was effected and sub-numbers was assigned even prior to the issue of 4(1) notification.

In response to the same,
Counsel for the appellant produced an endorsement issued by the Tahsildar on 29.07.2008 informing the plaintiffs that the documents sought for by them could not be issued as the authorities were not in a position to issue such a record from the mutilated records available in the office.
Therefore, it is clear that there is no material O.S.No.8098/2015 to show how and when the lands bearing Sy.No.112/12A and 112/11A came to sub- divided and sub-numbers were assigned.
The very existence of these lands is in question.
It these lands were in existence prior to the issuing of 4(1) notification, the same would have been shown in the notification while mentioning the boundaries of the acquired land.
Non mentioning of these lands in 4(1) notification also makes the version of the plaintiffs suspicious.
The trial court has also referred to the survey sketch prepared by the Taluk Surveyor, Bangalore South Taluk.
In the said document also, it is mentioned that only 4 guntas of land is situated adjoining the acquired land.

In such circumstances, the finding recorded by the trial court that no primafacie case was made out by the appellant and that the assertion of the plaintiff that they were in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property to an extent of 1 acre 12 guntas was not primafacie established cannot be regarded as illegal, O.S.No.8098/2015 perverse or capricious."
While perusing the above order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka the Hon'ble court specifically observed that Sy.No.112/12A and 112/11A are not in existence.
But while perusing last lines it is stated in operative portion that, "The observation made in judgment shall not come in the way of the final adjudication after controversy involved in the suit."

As per the observation made by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at the time when the notification was issued in the year 1983, there was no land bearing Sy.No.112/11A and 112/12A situated adjoining Sy.Nos.112/11 and 112/12.

Thus, it is cyrstal clear that, in the year 1983 there was no such land said by defendant bearing Sy.No.112/11A and 112/12A.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is a suit for permanent injunction by restraining the defendant, their men, agents, contractors,
workers or anybody claiming and acting under the defendants from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule property by the plaintiffs.
The Vijaya Bank Employees Housing Co-Operative Society Ltd formed a layout of sites by obtaning approved layout plan from the Bengaluru Development Authority.
The vendor of the plaintiffs were allotted with the said site as he was the member of the said Society.
It is executed a registered sale deed in favour of the vendor as per sale deed 28.02.1994 vide document Ramakantha Shetty P vs Srinivas on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80287660/
2 No.5074/93-94.
The plaintiffs have not executed any O.S.No.8098/2015 registered or unregistered document either in favour of the defendants or in favour of any their parties in respect of the schedule property.
The defendant No.1, 2 and 4 are brothers and they are the children of the defendant No.3.
They are total strangers to the schedule property and they have no manner of right, title and interest over the schedule property.
The defendants are claiming that they are the owners of the property situated on Western side of the schedule property.
The defendants without obtaining any plan or license from the competent authority are illegally making attempts to construct a building on the property situated on the western side of the suit schedule property and The caused of action for this suit arose on dated 18.09.2015 the defendant No.1 to 3 came near the Western adjacent property and they were taking measurements and in the said process they have attempted to encroach upon the schedule property on the Western side to an extent of 15 feet.
But the defendants threatened that they will continue their illegal acts and they will come back with more men and material.
The plaintiffs apprehend that the defendants may come at any time and encroach upon the schedule property and they may put up construction by encroaching upon the schedule property.
If they succeed in their attempts the loss and hardship caused to the plaintiffs cannot be compensated in terms of money.
The defendant No.3 filed written statement.
opennyai_summary.arguments: The plaintiffs are relying upon concocted and created documents and hence they are not entitled to any relief much less the one sought for in the suit.
opennyai_summary.issue:
8. On the above pleading of the parties, my predecessor in office has framed the following Issues:
1. Whether the plaintiffs prove their lawful possession over the suit property?
2. Do they prove the alleged obstruction of defendants?
3. Do they entitle for the relief of injunction as prayed for?
4. What order or decree?
9. After hearing arguments and considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, my findings on the above issues are here under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Negative Ramakantha Shetty P vs Srinivas on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80287660/
4  Issue No.2 : In the Negative  O.S.No.8098/2015  Issue No.3 : In the Negative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. ISSUE NOS.1 To 3 : These issues are taken together for discussion, since they are interconnected with each other and so also they require common discussion.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
After the O.S.No.8098/2015 Preliminary Notification, the owners of the land proposed to be acquired appeared to have made a representation to the acquiring body requesting for deletion of their lands or atleast the constructed portion in the land from the acquisition.
Based on this representation, while issuing the final notification dated 01.06.1985, only an extent of 27 guntas was acquired in Sy.No.112/11 excluding 11 guntas and in so far as Sy.No.112/12 is concerned, only an extent of 12 guntas came to be acquired excluding an extent of 15 guntas.
In the final notification, for the first time Sy.Nos.112/12A and 112/11A were shown as lands situated adjoining the acquired lands.
When the sub-division of these lands took place creating Sy.Nos.112/12A and 112/11A is not forthcoming from the records produced by the authorities.
Thus, it is crystal clear that land of defendant is in existence when the notification was published in the year 1985.
Hence, defendant proved that his land is in existence as per Ex.D.1.
When the vendor of plaintiff himself filed the suit stating that, his property was encroached by defendant he could have filed declaration and possession suit, but he filed bare injunction.
opennyai_summary.decision:
: In view of the findings on the above issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following :
O.S.No.8098/2015 O R D E R
The suit filed by the plaintiffs is hereby dismissed.
Draw decree accordingly.
